sentences.text:
By way of filing the present criminal misc. petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C.,
the petitioner has prayed for the following relief:-
"It is therefore, most respectfully and humbly prayed that this misc. petition may kindly be allowed and F.I.R. no. 349/2023 Police Station - Choupasni Housing Board, Jodhpur Metro (Rajasthan) may kindly be quashed and set aside."

entities.text: F.I.R. no. 349/2023 Police Station - Choupasni Housing Board, Jodhpur Metro (Rajasthan
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Learned counsel submitted that the petitioner is engaged in the business of sale and purchase of used cars in Jodhpur.

Drawing attention of the Court towards the impugned FIR, learned counsel submitted that the complainant-respondent No.2 herein purchased one preused Innova car bearing registration No. RJ-14- [2024:RJ-JD:21247] (2 of 5) [CRLMP-6653/2023] TB-4721 through the petitioner from its registered owner- Daulat Kanwar for a sale consideration of Rs.4,50,000/- vide agreement dated 30.11.2021.

At the time of sale of the above Innova car, the petitioner was informed that the same was purchased by its registered owner- Daulat Kanwar under Hypothecation Scheme (financed) vide agreement No.5441009 from one SK Finance Company.

The outstanding dues pertaining to the above vehicle have already been cleared off by Daulat Kanwar, therefore, the NOC Vinay Pratap Singh vs State Of Rajasthan on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75387042/
1 issued from SK Finance Company would be handed over to the petitioner within a period of 45 days of its purchase.

sentences.text: Learned counsel submitted that as per the impugned FIR, the petitioner after sale of the aforesaid vehicle, has breached the agreement/promise made to respondent No.2 as the petitioner has failed to provide the NOC from SK Finance Company to respondent No.2.
Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.

Learned counsel submitted that it is a settled law that in order to attract the provisions of Section 420 IPC, the prosecution not only has to prove that the accused has cheated someone but also by doing so, he has dishonestly induced the person who is so cheated to deliver the property.

There are three components of the offence under Section 420 IPC, i.e., (i) the deception of any person, (ii) fraudulently or dishonestly inducing that person to deliver any property to any person and (iii) mens rea or dishonest intention of accused at the time of making the inducement.

] Learned counsel submitted that in the present case, the sale was executed in the year 2021 and the FIR has been lodged in the year 2023 i.e after a delay of 2 years from the date of the alleged incident.

Learned counsel submitted that it is not in dispute that the possession of the vehicle No. RJ-14-TB-4721 was hand over to respondent No.2 in the year 2021 itself and thereafter, he started using the same.

Learned counsel further submitted that the petitioner cannot be made liable for the failure of the original registered owner/RC holder of the vehicle in question, in procuring the NOC from the finance company i.e. SK Finance Company.

Lastly, learned counsel drew attention of the Court towards the No Objection Certificate dated 31.01.2024 issued by SK Finance Company in the name of the registering authority, which indicates that Daulat Kanwar i.e. registered owner/RC holder of vehicle No. RJ-14-TB-4721 has fulfilled her entire liability and paid all of her outstanding dues under the said Hypothecation Agreement,
therefore, the company has no objection in case, registering authority undertakes any transfer instructions from Daulat Kanwar.
Learned counsel thus, prayed that since the petitioner has been implicated in a false criminal case, the impugned FIR may be quashed and set aside.

Per Contra, learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the prayer made on behalf of the petitioner and submitted that during the course of investigation, the offences under Section 426, 420 and 120-B IPC have been found to have been made out against the present petitioner.
[2024:RJ-JD:21247] (4 of 5) [CRLMP-6653/2023] Heard learned counsel for the parties at Bar.
Perused the material available on record.
It is not in dispute before this Court that the petitioner is dealing in sale and purchase of used cars.

The allegation against the present petitioner is that he has not handed over the NOC for removal of H.P.N. noting from registration certificate of vehicle No. RJ-14-TB-4721 which was purchased by respondent No.2 through the petitioner.
This Court finds that the vehicle No. RJ-14-TB-4721 was handed over to respondent No.2 on 30.11.2021 itself and thereupon, he started using the same.
The impugned FIR has been lodged after a delay of about 2 years from the date of purchase of the vehicle in question.

This Court on a close scrutiny of the documents available on record does not find any material available on record indicating that the petitioner knowingly furnished false information Vinay Pratap Singh vs State Of Rajasthan on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75387042/
2 relating to NOC of the vehicle in question to respondent No.2 or had an intention to cheat him from the very beginning.

sentences.text: As a matter of fact, it was the duty of the original registered owner/RC holder of the vehicle to have obtained the NOC from the SK Finance Company and handed it over to the petitioner.
Therefore, in the opinion of this Court, the alleged offences are not made out against the petitioner.

Consequently, the present criminal misc. petition is allowed; the impugned FIR No.349/2023,
registered at Police Station Choupasni Housing Board, Jodhpur (Metro) and all proceedings undertaken in pursuance thereof are hereby quashed and set aside.
[2024:RJ-JD:21247] (5 of 5) [CRLMP-6653/2023] Stay application and the other applications, if any, stand dismissed.
